selected_items.author: karpathy
selected_items.text: @ChrisJMcCormick Yeah, increasingly a lot more appealing to tear down these abstractions now that agents can do a lot of the math and drudgery and verification. A lot of the abstractions were built for a world with constraints of finite intelligence and attention in the industry.
selected_items.selection_reason: Special account (karpathy). Reply to Chris McCormick, who described writing model code as a single compilable forward_backward function with no autograd and no torch.nn abstractions, letting Claude write the backward math for the 24-layer nanochat architecture. Karpathy argues tearing down such abstractions is now appealing because agents handle the math and verification, and the abstractions were built for a world constrained by finite intelligence and attention.
selected_items.context_summary: Reply to ChrisJMcCormick's post about writing model code as a single compilable forward_backward function (no autograd, no torch.nn), with Claude writing the backward math for the 24-layer nanochat architecture.

selected_items.author: ns123abc
selected_items.text: OPENAI AND ANTHROPIC JUST FOLDED ON THEIR DATA RETENTION POLICY AFTER PALANTIR CEO EXPOSED THEIR REAL BUSINESS MODEL. Alex Karp: something has gone completely wrong; they want access to my data so they can build my alpha.
selected_items.selection_reason: Reports Palantir CEO Alex Karp criticising AI-lab data retention and the labs adjusting policy; company/policy move.

selected_items.author: MaxForAI
selected_items.text: Anthropic finally made official a feature that had been dragging on for nearly two years. Claude's Computer Use feature has been officially announced as launched. Computer Use was actually released as early as October 2024.
selected_items.selection_reason: Anthropic formally launches Claude Computer Use, nearly two years after its 2024 preview.

selected_items.author: MaxForAI
selected_items.text: Claude is gearing up to take on Google head-on. Anthropic officially launched Claude Academy, open to everyone for free. It offers courses from AI basics to using Claude, plus tutorials and use cases.
selected_items.selection_reason: Anthropic launches free Claude Academy learning platform. Distinct from Computer Use item.

selected_items.author: MParakhin
selected_items.text: Gisting is the most underappreciated LLM technique right now. It is basically zipping your prompt before running in production - it stops being human-readable, but is much smaller, runs much faster: ~40% lower E2E latency, ~15% higher throughput and the results are BETTER!
selected_items.selection_reason: Practitioner observation on prompt gisting for latency/throughput gains in production LLMs.

selected_items.author: jayair
selected_items.text: DeepSeek v4 Flash launched Aug 1st and within 2 weeks went from 3T tokens a day to 18T tokens a day on OpenCode; a 6x increase, close to doubling all other model usage on the platform.
selected_items.selection_reason: Reports DeepSeek v4 Flash usage growing 6x to 18T tokens/day on OpenCode; adoption data.

selected_items.author: agapekeleta
selected_items.text: I trained an LLM to remove AI slop and read more natural by matching how humans actually write. It can also remove the newly introduced statistical watermark embedded in Claude-generated text. Across my evaluation set, Pangram v4 classified every output as human-written.
selected_items.selection_reason: Practitioner reports a model that both de-slops text and strips Anthropic's text watermark, defeating a Pangram detector.

selected_items.author: danysvnt
selected_items.text: GOOGLE DEEPMIND CEO WARNS AI COULD GET OUT OF CONTROL IN THE NEXT 2-4 YEARS. Demis Hassabis on one of the things that worries him most: the AI itself going rogue or going off the rails, and he puts it at 2-4 years, not decades away.
selected_items.selection_reason: Hassabis warns of AI going rogue within 2-4 years; notable safety statement from a lab head.
